label: Backup task
type: the scheduled unit of execution a backup:plan produces - one of three task_type enum members (BACKUP/MERGE/PRUNE, siblings backup:merge-task and backup:prune-task) - as against cbbackupmgr, which has no 'task' object at all: an operator invokes a subcommand directly and it runs to completion, rather than being scheduled, paused or resumed as a persistent task.
evidence: To automate backups using the Backup Service, you must create a plan that tells the service what you want it to do.
You can still read the backed-up data in an archived repository. However, the Backup Service cannot perform further backups to the repository.
Note that neither resuming already running tasks nor pausing already paused tasks has any effect: both return `200 OK`.
Triggers an immediate backup for the specified active repository: thus, the need to wait for a scheduled backup can be eliminated as required.
note: Extraction-layer since round 19; crosses the promotion bar this round (backup-archive-a-repository.md, backup-create-and-edit-plans.md, backup-get-task-info.md, backup-pause-and-resume-tasks.md, backup-trigger-backup.md all reuse it in a relation slot). Pause/resume is Backup-Service-only vocabulary with no cbbackupmgr equivalent - a genuine capability the scheduler adds on top of the shared repository/task substrate, one of the strongest 'separate thing' data points this round found for the round's central CLI-vs-REST question.
relates_to_competency_question: What is the unit of scheduled execution in the Backup Service, and does cbbackupmgr have anything analogous?
